observations: A manual sewing machine is mounted on a wooden table with a metal frame.
The machine is black with gold-colored lettering and decorative elements.
The brand name 'SINGER' is visible in gold lettering on the front of the machine, above the needle area.
The machine has a large handwheel on the left side and a foot pedal mechanism below the table.
The table has a light wood top and a reddish-brown front panel.
The metal frame is dark, possibly painted or rusted, with a decorative footrest.
The machine appears to be in a used condition with some visible wear and minor scratches.
There is a watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI THAIBA' overlaid on the image.

claims.claim: Neatly use manual sewing machine is available for sale
claims.evidence: The machine appears used and has some wear, but 'neatly use' is subjective and not verifiable from the photo alone. No proof of condition beyond visual inspection.

risks.risk: The machine may not work or may have internal mechanical issues.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the machine in operation, including the handwheel turning and needle moving.

risks.risk: The machine may be missing parts (e.g., presser foot, bobbin case, or accessories).
risks.proof: A photo showing all included parts laid out or a video demonstrating the machine's full functionality.

risks.risk: The metal frame or table may be structurally unstable or rusted beyond repair.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the metal frame and joints, especially the footrest and legs, to check for rust or damage.

proof_requests: Video or photo of the machine in operation.
Photo showing all included parts and accessories.
Close-up of the metal frame and joints to check for rust or damage.
response.reason: The brand is identifiable as SINGER, but the condition and functionality cannot be confirmed from the single photo. The claim of 'neatly use' is subjective and unverified. Hidden risks include mechanical failure, missing parts, and structural damage to the frame, all of which require additional proof before pricing.
